title: Add large-state push benchmark
description:
Baseline benchmark so the `gopush` optimisations below can be measured rather than asserted.

## What

Extend `go/bench_test.go` with a realistic large-state fixture and benchmark the full push cycle:

- `Marshal` (the `MarshalFunc` path in `sync.go`)
- `mergePatcher.patch` (unmarshal + `objectDiff`)
- the no-change case (identical bytes) and the small-delta case (one leaf field changed)

## Fixture size and shape

Model it on the real rais-main `/api/state` capture — **341,817 bytes (342 KB)**, deeply nested maps and slices:

| key | bytes |
|---|---|
| `machines` | 277,156 |
| — `local` | 141,003 |
| — `cJI9lhUjtQ` | 85,132 |
| — `A9jexBGFhT` | 50,983 |
| `tools` | 38,080 |
| `config` | 6,193 |
| `chrome` | 5,662 |
| everything else | < 2,500 each |

Within the largest machine: `projects` 74,586 B, `toolConfig` 38,080 B, `terminals` 8,888 B, `agents` 6,109 B, `mcp` 3,589 B, `processTree` 3,443 B.

That shape matters — the win in task 4 comes from most of those bytes being unchanged between pushes.

## Measured baseline (Go 1.26.5, arm64, 341,817-byte payload)

| op | ns/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| `json.Unmarshal` → `map[string]any` | 8,402,363 | 1,585,544 | 34,014 |
| unmarshal + `objectDiff` (no change) | 10,896,244 | 1,629,906 | 34,942 |
| `bytes.Equal` on the same payload | 16,075 | 0 | 0 |

Decode throughput is only ~40 MB/s, so state size translates almost linearly into push cost.

## Why

In rais-main, `velox.(*State).gopush` is 66.7% of process CPU and 67% of allocated bytes — 309.63 MB of the 460.95 MB the process allocates per 30 s. Without a benchmark in-repo, every change here is unverifiable.
